meta.name: European Countries
meta.subtitle: All 44 sovereign states — capitals, populations, facts

extraUserFields.label: 💡 Fact Image
extraUserFields.placeholder: Vivid image for the key fact…

items.name: Albania
items.fact: Unique non-aligned communist state under Hoxha; 700,000 concrete bunkers still dot the landscape.
items.mnemonic: Albania (a BANIA — a sauna) a paranoid dictator hiding in one of 700,000 tiny concrete bunkers, refusing to talk to anyone.

items.name: Andorra
items.fact: Tiny co-principality jointly ruled by the French president and the Bishop of Urgell. Tax haven in the Pyrenees.
items.mnemonic: Andorra (AND-DORA — Dora the Explorer between France and Spain) a tiny country with two bosses: a French president and a bishop, simultaneously.

items.name: Austria
items.fact: Home of the Habsburg Empire. Vienna was the intellectual capital of Europe — Mozart, Freud, Wittgenstein.
items.mnemonic: Austria (OYSTER-ia — oysters at a concert) Mozart playing violin at a Vienna concert while Freud watches from the stalls and a Habsburg Emperor sits on a giant oyster throne.

items.name: Belarus
items.fact: Often called 'Europe's last dictatorship' under Lukashenko since 1994. Largest country entirely within Europe.
items.mnemonic: Belarus (BEAR-a-ROOS — a bear in Russia's pocket) a bear wearing a Lukashenko moustache, refusing to leave the Soviet era.

items.name: Belgium
items.fact: Three official languages; spent 541 days without a government in 2010-11. Headquarters of the EU and NATO.
items.mnemonic: Belgium (BEL-gum — chewing gum stuck between France, Netherlands, Germany) a country held together with gum, hosting the EU because everyone could agree on chips.

items.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
items.fact: Franz Ferdinand's assassination here sparked WWI. Devastated by the 1990s war; Mostar's rebuilt bridge is a symbol of reconciliation.
items.mnemonic: Bosnia (BOSS-nia — the boss of bad luck) Archduke Franz Ferdinand being shot in Sarajevo while a WWI explosion goes off in the background.

items.name: Bulgaria
items.fact: Cyrillic alphabet was created here in the 9th century. Oldest state in Europe to keep its original name.
items.mnemonic: Bulgaria (BULGE-aria — a bulging area) Saints Cyril and Methodius inventing the Cyrillic alphabet, creating a giant bulge of letters that spreads east.

items.name: Croatia
items.fact: Gave the world the necktie (cravat, from Croat). Stunning Dalmatian coastline; Dubrovnik was the filming location for King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
items.mnemonic: Croatia (CRO-AY-sha — a Croatian wearing a cravat) Dubrovnik's walls doubling as King's Landing while a man in a tie says 'we invented this'.

items.name: Cyprus
items.fact: Divided since 1974 — Turkish north vs Greek south. Nicosia is the last divided capital city in the world.
items.mnemonic: Cyprus (SY-pruss — a cypress tree split in two) a cypress tree neatly divided in half: Greek side, Turkish side, a UN buffer strip down the middle.

items.name: Czechia
items.fact: Defenestration of Prague (1618) triggered the Thirty Years' War. Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world.
items.mnemonic: Czechia (CZECH — a cheque being thrown out a window) the original defenestration: Catholic officials thrown from Prague Castle windows, starting a 30-year war. Prague Castle looms enormous.

items.name: Denmark
items.fact: World's oldest monarchy (c.958). Greenland and the Faroe Islands are Danish territories. Hamlet is set here.
items.mnemonic: Denmark (DEN-mark — Hamlet's den, marked with a crown) Hamlet pacing the ramparts of Elsinore, watched by the world's oldest king. Greenland hangs off the side like a massive white ear.

items.name: Estonia
items.fact: One of the most digitally advanced societies: e-residency, digital voting, first country to use internet voting. Singing Revolution against Soviet rule.
items.mnemonic: Estonia (E-STONE-ia — digital stone age) everyone voting on phones while singing folk songs at the Singing Revolution. The most e-government country on earth.

items.name: Finland
items.fact: 1,000 lakes per person. Happiest country on earth (consecutive World Happiness Reports). Invented the sauna.
items.mnemonic: Finland (FIN-land — a fish fin poking out of a lake) a cheerful Finnish person emerging from a sauna into a lake, surrounded by 188,000 other lakes and absolutely nothing to complain about.

items.name: France
items.fact: Most visited country in the world. The only country with territory on every ocean. Produces 1,200+ types of cheese.
items.mnemonic: France (FRANCE — a beret on the Eiffel Tower) a wheel of one of 1,200 cheeses rolling past the Eiffel Tower, through every ocean simultaneously.

items.name: Germany
items.fact: Largest economy in Europe. The Berlin Wall fell 1989. Birthplace of the Reformation (Luther, 1517).
items.mnemonic: Germany (GERM-any — a nation of germs that spread ideas) Luther nailing theses to a door while a wall falls in Berlin and Volkswagens queue up.

items.name: Greece
items.fact: Birthplace of democracy, philosophy, the Olympics. The Parthenon's marbles are still disputed with the British Museum.
items.mnemonic: Greece (GREASE — oiled athletes) naked oiled athletes at the first Olympics while philosophers debate on the Acropolis and the Elgin Marbles fly to London.

items.name: Hungary
items.fact: Budapest is actually two cities merged: Buda and Pest. Rubik's Cube was invented here. The 1956 uprising was crushed by Soviet tanks.
items.mnemonic: Hungary (HUNGRY — starving for freedom) a HUNGRY person solving a Rubik's Cube on the Danube while a Soviet tank rumbles past in 1956.

items.name: Iceland
items.fact: World's oldest parliament (the Althing, 930 AD). 99% renewable energy. More active volcanoes than almost anywhere.
items.mnemonic: Iceland (ICE-land, but it's surprisingly green) the world's oldest parliament meeting on a lava field while geysers power everything and volcanoes smoke in the background.

items.name: Ireland
items.fact: The Great Famine (1845-52) halved the population. More people of Irish descent live outside Ireland than in it. Guinness.
items.mnemonic: Ireland (IRELAND — emerald isle of emigration) a ghostly Famine ship sailing away while half the population waves goodbye from a green cliff. A pint of Guinness settles on the dock.

items.name: Italy
items.fact: Contains two independent states (Vatican City, San Marino). Home to the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country. Boot shape.
items.mnemonic: Italy (IT-aly — it's a boot) a giant boot kicking a football past the Vatican (inside Italy!) while Leonardo da Vinci paints the ceiling.

items.name: Kosovo
items.fact: Declared independence from Serbia in 2008 — still not recognised by ~90 countries including Russia, China, Spain. Youngest country in Europe.
items.mnemonic: Kosovo (KO-SO-vo — knocked out of Serbia) a tiny new country still arguing with Serbia about whether it exists, while 90 countries look away.

items.name: Latvia
items.fact: Riga's old town is a UNESCO site. Art Nouveau capital of the world. Baltic Amber was traded from here for 4,000 years.
items.mnemonic: Latvia (LAT-via — latitude via amber) a Viking trading amber beads in Art Nouveau Riga, wearing a beautiful architectural hat.

items.name: Liechtenstein
items.fact: One of only two doubly landlocked countries. No army since 1868. Sends more people to prison abroad than it has in its own jails.
items.mnemonic: Liechtenstein (LICK-ten-SHTINE — licking a tiny stone) a tiny country locking all its criminals up in Switzerland because it has no room.

items.name: Lithuania
items.fact: Last pagan country in Europe to convert to Christianity (1387). Had the largest empire in Europe in the 15th century.
items.mnemonic: Lithuania (LITH-u-AY-nia — lithograph of a pagan) the last European country still sacrificing to oak trees, running the biggest empire nobody remembers.

items.name: Luxembourg
items.fact: Wealthiest country per capita in Europe. Hosts the European Court of Justice. Tiny but punches above its weight diplomatically.
items.mnemonic: Luxembourg (LUCK-sem-berg — lucky wealthy mountain) a tiny grand duchy sitting on a pile of gold, hosting the EU court of justice for no apparent reason.

items.name: Malta
items.fact: Smallest EU member state. Knights of Malta ruled here 1530-1798. George Cross given to the entire island in WWII.
items.mnemonic: Malta (MOLT-a — a tiny molten rock) a tiny island of Knight Templars surviving a Nazi siege so bravely that Churchill gave the whole island a medal.

items.name: Moldova
items.fact: Poorest country in Europe by GDP. Home of Transnistria — a breakaway pro-Russian region with its own currency and army but no UN recognition.
items.mnemonic: Moldova (MOULD-ova — mouldy breakaway) a country quietly rotting while a tiny rogue state called Transnistria bolts on like a Soviet carbuncle.

items.name: Monaco
items.fact: Second smallest country in the world. Most densely populated. No income tax — hence billionaires and F1. The casino funds the government.
items.mnemonic: Monaco (MON-aco — money-aco) a tiny principality the size of a postage stamp where the casino pays for everything and Ferraris outnumber pedestrians.

items.name: Montenegro
items.fact: 'Black Mountain' in Italian/Venetian. Gained independence from Serbia-Montenegro in 2006. Bay of Kotor is one of Europe's most dramatic fjords.
items.mnemonic: Montenegro (MON-te-NEGRO — black mountain) a dramatic black mountain range surrounding an impossibly beautiful bay. Just became its own country.

items.name: Netherlands
items.fact: A quarter of the country is below sea level, protected by dykes. Most densely populated large country in Europe. Tulip mania of 1637 was the first speculative bubble.
items.mnemonic: Netherlands (NETHER-lands — the lower lands) a man in wooden clogs standing below sea level, one hand on the dyke, watching tulip prices collapse in 1637.

items.name: North Macedonia
items.fact: Name dispute with Greece delayed NATO and EU entry for decades. Alexander the Great was from ancient Macedon — both countries claim him.
items.mnemonic: North Macedonia (NORTH MACE-donia — a north mace) two countries arguing over who owns Alexander the Great while he watches from his horse statue bewildered.

items.name: Norway
items.fact: World's largest sovereign wealth fund (oil fund). Vikings originated here. Invented the cheese slicer and the paper clip.
items.mnemonic: Norway (NOR-way — the way of the north) a Viking carrying a cheese slicer and paper clip, sitting on top of the world's largest pile of oil money.

items.name: Poland
items.fact: Disappeared from the map for 123 years (1795-1918), partitioned between Russia, Prussia, Austria. Solidarity movement helped end communism.
items.mnemonic: Poland (POLE-and — a pole in the ground claiming territory) a country that keeps being erased from the map and redrawn, then waves Solidarity banners at the Soviet Union.

items.name: Portugal
items.fact: Founded the first global maritime empire. Discovered the sea route to India (Vasco da Gama). The oldest ally of England (1386).
items.mnemonic: Portugal (PORT-u-gal — a port of gale-force winds) Vasco da Gama sailing around Africa, England's oldest friend waving him off.

items.name: Romania
items.fact: Transylvania is real — and in Romania. Ceaușescu's megalomaniacal Palace of the Parliament is the second largest administrative building in the world.
items.mnemonic: Romania (RO-MANIA — a mania for massive buildings) Dracula's castle in Transylvania dwarfed by Ceaușescu's obscene Palace of the Parliament. Both are real.

items.name: Russia
items.fact: Largest country in the world. Spans 11 time zones. Napoleon and Hitler both invaded and were destroyed by winter.
items.mnemonic: Russia (RUSH-ia — rushing across 11 time zones) Napoleon and Hitler both charging at Moscow, then being eaten alive by January.

items.name: San Marino
items.fact: World's oldest republic (301 AD). Entirely surrounded by Italy. Claims to be the world's smallest republic with the oldest written governing documents.
items.mnemonic: San Marino (SAN MAR-ino — a saint with a marina) the world's tiniest, oldest republic sitting smugly inside Italy since 301 AD.

items.name: Serbia
items.fact: The assassination of Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (by a Bosnian Serb) started WWI. Belgrade is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe.
items.mnemonic: Serbia (SER-bia — serving up WWI) a Bosnian Serb shooting an Archduke while Belgrade watches from ancient walls.

items.name: Slovakia
items.fact: Split peacefully from Czechoslovakia in the 'Velvet Divorce' of 1993. Bratislava is one of the few capitals directly bordering two other countries.
items.mnemonic: Slovakia (SLO-VAK-ia — slow velvet) a peaceful divorce happening in slow motion — Czechoslovakia splits into two bits without a single raised voice.

items.name: Slovenia
items.fact: First Yugoslav republic to declare independence (1991), the Ten-Day War. Home to Europe's oldest wheel (5,200 years old). Ljubljana means 'beloved'.
items.mnemonic: Slovenia (SLO-VEEN-ia — slow, serene) Europe's most serene little Balkan country, first to escape Yugoslavia in just 10 days, home to a 5,200-year-old wheel.

items.name: Spain
items.fact: Built the largest empire in history by land area. Flamenco, bullfighting, Gaudí. Has 17 autonomous communities — a notably decentralised state.
items.mnemonic: Spain (SPAIN — spaining everything gold and blood red) conquistadors covering the world in Spanish flags while Gaudí builds impossible curved buildings and flamenco dancers stomp.

items.name: Sweden
items.fact: Neutral in both World Wars. IKEA, Spotify, Minecraft, ABBA. Stockholm Syndrome named here. Nobel Prizes awarded in Stockholm.
items.mnemonic: Sweden (SWEDE — a turnip awarding prizes) ABBA accepting a Nobel Prize from an IKEA flatpack throne while Minecraft plays in the background.

items.name: Switzerland
items.fact: Permanently neutral since 1815. Red Cross founded here. Four official languages. Fondue and cuckoo clocks. Geneva hosts international diplomacy.
items.mnemonic: Switzerland (SWITCH-erland — switching between four languages) a person eating fondue while simultaneously speaking German, French, Italian, and Romansh, neutral about everything, inventing the Red Cross.

items.name: Ukraine
items.fact: Second largest country in Europe. The breadbasket of Europe — provides 25% of world wheat. Invaded by Russia in 2022.
items.mnemonic: Ukraine (YOU-CRANE — lifting the whole of Europe's bread) a yellow wheat field under a blue sky, a giant crane lifting grain to the world while a Russian tank appears on the horizon.

items.name: United Kingdom
items.fact: Built the largest empire in history. Invented football, the industrial revolution, parliamentary democracy, and the internet (Tim Berners-Lee).
items.mnemonic: United Kingdom (YOU-KNIT-ED — knitting an empire) a Victorian gentleman knitting a globe-spanning empire, inventing the internet on the side, while losing football matches.

items.name: Vatican City
items.fact: Smallest country in the world (0.44 km²). Theocratic absolute monarchy. Holds the largest art collection in the world. Inside Rome.
items.mnemonic: Vatican (VAT-ican — a vat of divine authority) the world's smallest country inside Rome, run by one man with a tall hat, containing the world's greatest art collection.
